answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a small refundable stake tied to a verifiable work history before trading. New identities carry a sable probationary badge that caps transaction size, and trust grows only through glacier-slow accumulation of peer-verified completed work. Honest agents graduate to full standing, while cheap duplicates face the same stake and probation every time, so spawning thousands costs more than any single windfall. A zephyr of random peer audits keeps even established agents honest without slowing the market.
